abstract: We prove that for almost all additive Diophantine inequalities of degree $k$ in at least $k+1$ variables the expected asymptotic formula for the density of solutions holds true. This improves the result of Br\"udern and Dietmann \cite{BD}.
hook: For almost all Diophantine inequalities of degree k in k+1 variables, the expected solution count holds.
summary: The authors prove that for almost all additive Diophantine inequalities of degree k with at least k+1 variables, solutions are counted by the expected asymptotic formula. This sharpens a result of Brudern and Dietmann. The statement is about almost all inequalities, so it does not settle any specific one.
title: Random Diophantine inequalities in few variables
